<a id="the-least-loss-as-a-premise-of-rest--最小损失作为停息的前提"></a>
# The least loss as a premise of rest

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`least-loss-rest` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](least-loss-rest.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> In Archimedean amounts a closed amount approaches rest with no least loss: few steps lose at least any ε above nothing. Rest needs a least loss at each change counted: halving approaches rest and never reaches it. Whole numbers are the instance with ε one; a loss needs a law that merges.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Amounts: an addition, associative and commutative with nothing as its unit, and an order that addition keeps and that cancels, with nothing least; no amount need be a whole number, and the order may be dense. The order is a preorder, so no quotient is taken. (`Becoming.Amounts`, `Becoming.Amounts.times`, `Becoming.Amounts.sum`, `Becoming.Amounts.add_zero`, `Becoming.Amounts.le_of_eq`, `Becoming.Amounts.add_le_add_left`, `Becoming.Amounts.le_add_right`, `Becoming.Amounts.le_add_left`, `Becoming.Amounts.add_swap`, `Becoming.Amounts.times_le`)
2. The loss law: where across each step from T on the amount after the step, with the step's loss, is within the amount before, the losses since T, added, are within the amount at T. No least loss is named; the losses of a falling stock are summable in any amounts. (`Becoming.Amounts.losses_within`)
3. The least-loss law of rest: where an amount does not rise from T on, falls by at least ε across each step at which P holds, and m copies of ε are not within its value at T, steps at which P holds do not recur; with the premises read as far as can be refuted, it is not the case that after every step a later such step stays unrefuted. The premises are the least loss ε and the bound of the stock by finitely many copies of it. (`Becoming.Amounts.still_le`, `Becoming.Amounts.loses_times`, `Becoming.Amounts.rests_unrefuted`, `Becoming.Amounts.rests`)
4. In Archimedean amounts every amount lies within finitely many copies of any amount above nothing, so a least loss above nothing alone brings rest. (`Becoming.Amounts.Archimedean`, `Becoming.Amounts.rests_of_archimedean`)
5. The approach to rest, with no least loss: where across each step from T on the amount after the step, with the step's loss, is within the amount before, then for any k steps f 0 < f 1 < … from T on, each losing at least ε, k copies of ε are within the amount at T; so where m copies are not, fewer than m steps lose at least ε, a bound on the count with no decision. In Archimedean amounts such an m exists for every ε above nothing: a closed amount comes arbitrarily near rest, and steps losing at least ε do not recur. The Archimedean property is the one structural premise. In whole numbers approach is rest: no more steps lose anything than the stock counts. (`Becoming.Amounts.still_within`, `Becoming.Amounts.still_of_falls`, `Becoming.Amounts.large_losses_from`, `Becoming.Amounts.large_losses_within`, `Becoming.Amounts.few_large_losses`, `Becoming.Amounts.few_large_losses_of_archimedean`, `Becoming.Amounts.approaches_rest`, `Becoming.Amounts.whole_losing_steps`)
6. A family at rest in any amounts: where from T on the stock after a step with the uptake is within the stock before with the replenishment, the replenishment is within the uptake, at each step at which P holds the replenishment with ε is, and the stock at T lies within fewer than m copies of ε, steps at which P holds do not recur. (`Becoming.Amounts.family_still`, `Becoming.Amounts.family_loses`, `Becoming.Amounts.family_rests`, `Becoming.Amounts.family_rests_of_archimedean`)
7. More without end needs replenishment without bound, in any Archimedean amounts with a least take: where a family is balanced and its uptake, from some step on, is at least every multiple of a least take ε above nothing, no bound within finitely many copies of ε holds of its replenishment. The whole-number law Flow.More.replenishment_unbounded_from is proved as its instance (each taker takes at least one). Without a least take it fails: with halving takes, 2^(t+1) takers each take 1/2^(t+1) at the step from t, so the takers are more without end, every take is above nothing, and one whole given at each step balances them. (`Becoming.Amounts.replenishment_unbounded`, `Becoming.Flow.More.replenishment_unbounded_from`, `Becoming.Halving.times_le_num`, `Becoming.Halving.le_two_pow`, `Becoming.Halving.one`, `Becoming.Halving.takes_within_one`, `Becoming.Halving.takes_halve`)
8. Whole numbers are the instance: the least loss is one and every stock lies within its own count of ones plus one, and whole numbers are Archimedean. The rest family is proved as this instance, below the modules that state it: the spine's two descents falls_not_recurring (Becoming.Renewal) and falls_stop_unrefuted (Becoming.Space), Flow.taking_not_recurring_from and Flow.takers_within_on (Becoming.Dissipation) and Flow.change_stops_unrefuted (Becoming.Openness), through which the rest theorem World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed follows. (`Becoming.Amounts.whole`, `Becoming.Amounts.whole_times_one`, `Becoming.Amounts.whole_within`, `Becoming.Amounts.whole_archimedean`, `Becoming.Amounts.whole_sum`, `Becoming.falls_not_recurring`, `Becoming.falls_stop_unrefuted`, `Becoming.Flow.taking_not_recurring_from`, `Becoming.Flow.takers_within_on`, `Becoming.Flow.change_stops_unrefuted`, `Becoming.World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed`)
9. Without a least loss: dyadic amounts are dense, every amount above nothing having its half below it and above nothing, and Archimedean; a stock halving in them at every step loses at every step, no amount above nothing is within every loss, and it never rests. (`Becoming.Dyadic`, `Becoming.mul_assoc_nat`, `Becoming.add_mul_split`, `Becoming.Naturals.mul_right_comm`, `Becoming.mul_turn`, `Becoming.Naturals.pow_add`, `Becoming.Dyadic.ext'`, `Becoming.Dyadic.add`, `Becoming.Dyadic.le`, `Becoming.Dyadic.zero`, `Becoming.Dyadic.le_trans'`, `Becoming.Dyadic.add_assoc'`, `Becoming.Dyadic.add_comm'`, `Becoming.Dyadic.zero_add'`, `Becoming.Dyadic.expand`, `Becoming.Dyadic.add_le_add_right'`, `Becoming.Dyadic.le_of_add_le_add_right'`, `Becoming.Dyadic.zero_le'`, `Becoming.Dyadic.amounts`, `Becoming.Dyadic.num_pos`, `Becoming.Dyadic.half_below`, `Becoming.Dyadic.times_ge`, `Becoming.Dyadic.archimedean`, `Becoming.Halving.stock`, `Becoming.Halving.loss`, `Becoming.Halving.falls`, `Becoming.Halving.loss_positive`, `Becoming.Halving.no_least_loss`, `Becoming.Halving.falls_strictly`, `Becoming.Halving.never_rests`, `Becoming.Halving.approaches_without_reaching`)
10. Without the bound by least losses: in layered amounts, a coarse dyadic layer and a fine whole-number layer counting only where the coarse layers agree, a stock falls by a least loss of one fine unit at every step, lies beyond every multiple of it, and never rests. (`Becoming.Layered`, `Becoming.Layered.ext'`, `Becoming.Layered.add`, `Becoming.Layered.le`, `Becoming.Layered.zero`, `Becoming.Layered.le_trans'`, `Becoming.Layered.add_le_add_right'`, `Becoming.Layered.le_of_add_le_add_right'`, `Becoming.Layered.amounts`, `Becoming.Layered.stock`, `Becoming.Layered.least`, `Becoming.Layered.least_positive`, `Becoming.Layered.loses`, `Becoming.Layered.times_coarse`, `Becoming.Layered.beyond_every_multiple`, `Becoming.Layered.never_rests`, `Becoming.Layered.not_archimedean`)
11. Rest and return: over finitely many configurations a law that merges nothing returns every configuration, so an amount that does not rise along an orbit is at its start within its value at every step, and where it falls by a loss at each step every loss is nothing. A loss above nothing needs a law that merges: the least loss on which rest turns is a premise of descriptions that lump configurations and dissipate, and a finite law that merges nothing returns rather than rests. (`Becoming.Law.Lossless.regains`, `Becoming.Law.Lossless.loses_nothing`, `Becoming.Law.loss_needs_merge`, `Becoming.Branching.Lossless.loses_nothing`, `Becoming.Branching.loss_needs_merge`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. The least loss ε at each step at which P holds and the bound of the stock at T by m copies of ε are hypotheses of Amounts.rests, Amounts.rests_unrefuted and Amounts.family_rests; in Archimedean amounts the bound follows from ε above nothing, and the approach law asks only the Archimedean property. The amounts' eleven laws are the fields of Amounts; antisymmetry, totality and decidability of the order are not asked.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Flow, Web and World with levels in any amounts: the step the rest laws turn on is stated for any amounts, not those structures over any amounts.
- That any physical system has a least loss per change; the statistical second law names none, and which physical premises supply one is stated, as a correspondence, in least-loss-from-entropy-production (T1).
- Real numbers; dyadic amounts witness density in the core, and the reals are not constructed.
- That coming to rest supports or damages 生生.
- **Counterexample:** Halving.never_rests: dense, Archimedean dyadic amounts, every loss above nothing and no least loss, the stock falling at every step. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/LeastLoss.lean)
- **Counterexample:** Layered.never_rests: a least loss at every step, the stock beyond every multiple of it, falling at every step; the amounts are not Archimedean (Layered.not_archimedean), so approach fails too. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/LeastLoss.lean)
- **Counterexample:** Halving.approaches_without_reaching: the halving stock approaches rest, few steps losing at least any ε above nothing, and falls at every step, as exponential relaxation does. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/LeastLoss.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** Stated for discrete steps. · No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

The outside review of 19 October 2026 (R20) and an outside reader named the rest laws' dependence on whole-number amounts as the main gap between the spine and our universe: with real-valued amounts losses can shrink geometrically. Reading (the AI's): what the whole numbers carry is a floor on the cost of each change counted, and the stock's being finitely many floors deep; where change has no floor a closed system can change ever more slightly for ever without exhausting what it has.

### Dependencies

  - Output: Dissipated on, a family's replenishment with its takers is within its uptake.

There a law that merges nothing returns every configuration within finitely many; here that return makes every loss along an orbit nothing, so the least loss of the rest laws needs a law that merges (Law.Lossless.loses_nothing, Law.loss_needs_merge).
- related, not a proved adapter: [rest-at-every-resolution](rest-at-every-resolution.md). There the unit may split and the same boundary is read at a refining unit (Asymptote, Dwindle); here amounts have no unit and the least loss is a premise.
- related, not a proved adapter: [rest-with-refinement-counted](rest-with-refinement-counted.md). There counting the refinement brings rest at every resolution with no premise added; here the premise whole numbers supplied is named for amounts with no unit.
